crime.value: Two razor throat murders: Gabrielle Marchant killed in her apartment; later, Leona Tasker killed in identical fashion. Central question: who committed these murders and why?
crime.quote: She was all cut up... The murderer was right-handed... reached across her right shoulder and simply drew the razor across her throat.

victim.value: Gabrielle Marchant: beautiful divorcee with multiple lovers including Noel Tasker. Killable because her romantic entanglements (jealousy, rejection) and Leona's discovery of infidelity provided motive.
victim.quote: Gabrielle Marchant! His Gaby!... she had plenty of men. All Gaby had ever seemed to want was a good time.

closed_world.value: Camelot Court apartment complex where both victims lived in adjacent buildings; a bounded residential community where movements and arrivals are observable to neighbors.
closed_world.quote: He drove through the entrance of Camelot Court and took the left drive... There were four vehicles parked before her door today, three police cruisers and a white ambulance.

culprit_and_motive.value: Noel Tasker murdered Leona (his wife) for $50,000 insurance and freedom; Leona murdered Gabrielle from jealous rage upon discovering her husband's affair. Noel frames the crimes as work of a 'maniac.'
culprit_and_motive.quote: Impersonate the maniac, or let it look like a rational crime, a husband murdering his wife for a rational motive, fifty thousand dollars.

resolution.value: Lieutenant Kabrick discovers Leona's fingerprint on the coffee table and ashtray at Leona's murder scene matches the fingerprint on the razor from Marchant's murder. Kabrick deduces: Leona killed Marchant; Noel killed Leona.
resolution.quote: A print of your wife's, on the table and on the tray, matched the print on the razor in the Marchant apartment... if your wife killed Marchant, who killed your wife?

investigator.value: Lieutenant Kabrick: official homicide detective who methodically reconstructs the crime through forensic evidence (fingerprints, blood patterns, M.O. analysis) and interrogation.
investigator.quote: Lieutenant Kabrick slouched in the depths of the chair and smiled... In Homicide you have to theorize. There's this matter of the blood.
